subject: Novex Health launch: temporary ratebook exception and traffic forecast
messages:
From: Lauren King <lauren.king@novexhealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Launch spike request: temporary ratebook increase for initial week

Hi Priyom,

We have a hard launch scheduled for Sept 2 and expect a concentrated traffic window in the first 72 hours as we flip the feature flag. Early projections show peak API ingest roughly 6x our current trial volumes for that window. Can Redwood provide a temporary ratebook increase (short-term carveout) to avoid 429s while we warm up?

Key asks:
- Temporary spike allowance for 72 hours starting Sept 2 PDT (target peak concurrent qps and token rates attached)
- Clear guardrails: what thresholds trigger throttling or soft-fails?
- Any impact to SLA or cost uplift estimates

I attached our internal traffic sheet for reference. Happy to jump on a short call.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren King
Head of Platform, Novex Health
lauren.king@novexhealth.com

Date: 2026-08-12T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Launch spike request: temporary ratebook increase for initial week

Team — forwarding Novex ask. High level here: they need a short-lived bump for launch day + 72h. Can product/ops confirm what we can reasonably support without changing their tier (hosted account)?

Questions I have for the group:
- Required peak qps and token/sec from the attached sheet (I opened their upload). Is this within our transient headroom or do we recommend dedicated fallback?
- What limits do we want to set for a temporary carveout (per-minute, per-user, model-level caps)?
- Risk: are there model-variant incompatibilities that would force fallback and increase latency?
- Billing: how do we surface cost uplift to the customer and get procurement sign-off fast?

I attached a cleaned projection we can edit and send to the customer. Please reply with concrete numbers today if possible — Novex is pushing on sign-off timelines.

Thanks,
Priyom

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-13T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch spike request: temporary ratebook increase for initial week

Thanks for the ping. I reviewed the projection and ran a quick capacity check with infra. Summary:

- Customer peak profile: ~6x baseline for first 72 hours, with a tailing 48h at ~2x. Total token/s demand concentrated in the 6-hour window post-flip.
- Infrastructure: hosted pool has short-term slack to absorb ~3x spikes across the region without dedicated reservation. Beyond that, we'd need either temporary reserved capacity (dedicated nodes) or firm rate limits.

Proposal for a safe carveout we can approve quickly:
- 72-hour temporary window starting 2026-09-02T00:00 PDT
- Soft-rate increments: allow bursts up to 4x baseline for 10 minutes, with a cap at sustained 2.5x averaged over 30 minutes to protect other tenants
- Model-level guardrail: restrict high-cost model variants (gpt-xl-16k-q8) during the burst window; auto-fallback to gpt-large-8k if latencies exceed 400ms
- Cost uplift: estimate +42% token cost for the 72-hour window; we should present this as an estimated uplift in the SOW

Action items for product/ops:
- Marissa: can you confirm the auto-fallback policy and whether we can enforce model-level caps per account for a defined window?
- Neha: can you draft the temporary entitlement and payment note to procurement language (we should require acknowledgement of the uplift)
- Priyom: I can spin up a quick dedicated pool if customer signs a short commit; need lead time 48 hours.

Karthik
Director, Product Ops
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch spike request: temporary ratebook increase for initial week

Looping in specifics after quick simulation. I ran their numbers through our traffic model and attached the enforcement form. Highlights:

- With the proposed soft increments, system-wide impact is acceptable for a single region (us-west). Headroom is tight if other major customers spike the same day, so we should scope the carveout to the account and add emergency rollback clauses.
- We can implement per-account model caps for the window and the fallback gating Karthik proposed. Engineering can push the policy through the runtime config in ~6 business hours.
- I attached a temporary exemption form that procurement will need signed plus an acceptance checkbox confirming they understand cost uplift and rollback conditions.

Recommend we present Novex with two options:
1) No-commit temporary carveout (as Karthik outlined) with the cost uplift estimate;
2) 48-hour reserved capacity commit for a reduced uplift (we price this and it requires an expedite PO).

Next steps: Priyom, if you want me to send option copy to Novex I can. Otherwise we need their decision by Aug 24 to guarantee any dedicated pool prep.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-08-18T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch spike request: temporary ratebook increase for initial week

Hi Lauren and Sam — thanks for the patience. Quick summary and options so you can decide and we can finalize paperwork: 

Option A — Short carveout (no commit)- Window: 72 hours starting 2026-09-02T00:00 PDT- Burst policy: up to 4x baseline for 10 minutes; sustained cap 2.5x averaged over 30 minutes- Model gating: fallback to gpt-large-8k for bursted requests; high-cost variants suppressed- Cost: estimated +42% token bill for the window- Proc: sign temp-rate-exemption-form (attached), accept rollback clause

Option B — Short reserved pool (48-hour commit)- Window prep: needs PO/commit by 2026-08-24 to allow 48h provisioning- Benefit: lower uplift (we will provide a firm price in the SOW) and tighter latency guarantees

Next steps:
- If you pick A, please sign the exemption form and upload to the DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/templates/abc123
- If you pick B, we need a one-page PO or written commit to procure@redwood.com by Aug 24; I will route to capacity for provisioning.
- HubSpot: I logged this as HS-23456 and attached the cleaned projection. Drive link and SOW draft here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1xExample

Happy to jump on a 15-min call tomorrow to walk through options.
